title: Risdon Cove and the Black War

draft.title: Risdon Cove and the Black War
card: In 1804 the British set up a small settlement at Risdon Cove, on the Derwent River in Van Diemen's Land, now called Tasmania. The land was Aboriginal land, and Aboriginal people hunted there.

In May 1804 a group of Aboriginal people was near the settlement. Soldiers fired on them, and a number of Aboriginal people were killed. Historians still debate how many died and why the shooting began.
As more colonists arrived, they took more land and hunting grounds. Fighting grew in the 1820s, and the conflict is now called the Black War.
Aboriginal people of Tasmania suffered heavy losses from violence and disease. Their numbers fell sharply, but Aboriginal Tasmanians survived, and their descendants and culture continue today.
draft.remember: Risdon Cove in 1804 began a pattern of violence, and the Black War of the 1820s brought heavy losses to Aboriginal Tasmanians, who survive today.

a.q: What happened at Risdon Cove in 1804?
opts: Soldiers fired on a group of Aboriginal people
Aboriginal people drove the British out of Tasmania
The British and Aboriginal people signed a treaty
Aboriginal people attacked the first ships to arrive
a.why: At Risdon Cove soldiers fired on Aboriginal people near the new settlement. No treaty was signed, and the British were not driven out. The settlement was the start of British occupation of that land.

b.q: In the 1820s, more colonists in Van Diemen's Land took land and hunting grounds. What was the result?
opts: Fighting grew into the conflict called the Black War
Aboriginal people gained legal ownership of the land
The colonists left the island because of the fighting
Aboriginal people were safe because they moved away
b.why: As colonists took more land, conflict increased and became known as the Black War. It left Aboriginal Tasmanians with heavy losses. Colonists did not leave, and Aboriginal people were not given ownership of land.
b.clue: Think about what taking hunting grounds did to relations.

a.best: Soldiers fired on a group of Aboriginal people

b.best: Fighting grew into the conflict called the Black War

problems.detail: The Risdon Cove settlement was set up in September 1803 under Lieutenant John Bowen, not in 1804. The shooting took place in May 1804. The first card line should say 1803.
The remember line says Risdon Cove 'began a pattern of violence'. The card makes no such causal claim; it only says fighting grew later as more colonists arrived.
The clue 'Who fired, and on whom?' gives the answer away. The right option is the only one that mentions firing, so a student can pick it without knowing what happened.
